# APEX Core
## Agentic Platform for Enterprise eXecution — Core Framework Build Specification

**Spec version:** 1.0
**Target audience:** Claude Code (primary build agent) · APEX SteerCo · DMTSP engagement teams
**Structural alignment:** AXLE framework conventions
**Deliverable class:** Abstract framework — conventions, design system, shared data, reusable render components
**Relationship:** Parent spec to edition specs (APEX-RC, APEX-TH, APEX-FS, ...)

---

## Part 0 — Compliance & Language Constraints (Non-Negotiable)

**These rules apply to every asset generated by this build and every edition that inherits from APEX Core.**

**Never use** "partner," "alliance," or "strategic alliance" to describe the Deloitte–Microsoft relationship, in any tense or compound form.

**Approved substitutes:**
- "Deloitte's Microsoft practice"
- "DMTSP"
- "Microsoft platform capabilities"
- "Microsoft-native deployment"
- "Deloitte's Microsoft-aligned solution engineering"

**Out of scope for client-facing copy:** internal Deloitte engagement mechanics — ECIF, ACO routing specifics, Independence constraints, SI pass-through arrangements. Reference only in operational/technology-neutral terms if they appear at all.

**PII & customer data:** Any demo or seed data must be synthetic. Identifiers must be clearly fictional.

**Inheritance rule:** Every edition (APEX-RC, APEX-TH, etc.) inherits these constraints. No edition may override, soften, or exempt.

---

## Part 1 — What APEX Is

APEX (Agentic Platform for Enterprise eXecution) is a domain-canonical reference framework for deploying agentic AI systems on Microsoft-native infrastructure. APEX Core defines the abstract framework — the grammar that every industry edition inherits.

**APEX Core is not a deliverable to clients.** It is the framework-of-frameworks that DMTSP teams use to produce industry-specific editions. Clients see an edition (APEX-RC, APEX-TH, APEX-FS), not Core.

### 1.1 What Core defines

1. **Structural conventions** — numbering, naming, grammar that every edition follows
2. **Shared content** — industry-agnostic concepts (AI Journey Eras, CMM stages)
3. **Design system** — typography, color tokens, layout, motion, theme behavior
4. **Reusable render components** — widgets consumed by every edition site

### 1.2 What Core does not define

1. **Industry-specific forces, schemas, agents, orchestrations** — that's the edition's job
2. **Reference implementations** — those live under their edition
3. **Commercial content** — client-facing collateral belongs to editions

### 1.3 Relationship to AXLE

AXLE is a cross-industry reference framework that predates APEX. APEX Core adopts AXLE's structural conventions so that anyone fluent in AXLE recognizes APEX's grammar immediately: same Forces of Change framing, same AI Journey Eras, same Commercial Maturity Model, same medallion architecture, same numbered orchestrations, same ISV Ecosystem treatment, same wave-based deployment. Where AXLE defines a convention, APEX Core inherits it.

---

## Part 2 — Edition Model

### 2.1 The inheritance contract

Every APEX edition:

1. **Inherits** Part 0 compliance constraints (immutable)
2. **Inherits** Parts 3–7 structural conventions (extend, don't replace)
3. **Inherits** Part 9 design system (may extend tokens, must not break theme behavior)
4. **Inherits** Part 10 reusable render components
5. **Populates** its own forces, schemas, agents, orchestrations, ISV ecosystem, waves, reference implementations
6. **Conforms** to Part 11 acceptance criteria for editions

### 2.2 Edition naming convention

- Folder: `apex-<code>/` (lowercase)
- Short code: `APEX-<CODE>` (uppercase), where `<CODE>` is a 2–3 character industry code
- Full name: "APEX · <Industry Full Name> Edition"

**Registered edition codes:**

| code | full name | status |
|---|---|---|
| RC | Retail & Consumer | Active build |
| TH | Travel & Hospitality | Active build |
| FS | Financial Services | Reserved |
| LS | Life Sciences | Reserved |
| EN | Energy | Reserved |
| MF | Manufacturing | Reserved |
| PS | Public Sector | Reserved |

### 2.3 Cross-edition content reuse

When two editions need the same concept with an industry-specific flavor (e.g., both RC and TH have a "Customer Experience" schema but with different grains), **do not reuse the JSON**. Each edition owns its own content. The grammar is shared; the content is not.

When two editions need **exactly** the same content (e.g., AI Journey Eras, CMM stages, design tokens), the content lives in APEX Core and both editions import it.

---

## Part 3 — Forces of Change (Framing Convention)

Forces of Change are the structural drivers that define the operating environment for an industry at a point in time. Every edition defines its own.

### 3.1 Convention

- Each edition defines **6–10 forces**
- Each force has: `id` (FOC-NN), `force` (name), `signal` (observable indicator), `implication` (agentic deployment consequence)
- Forces are numbered within each edition (FOC-01 through FOC-NN)
- Forces are rendered in the edition site as a grid or a numbered list

### 3.2 Entity template

```
id            FOC-NN
force         VARCHAR(80)
signal        VARCHAR(400) — observable, measurable signal
implication   VARCHAR(400) — consequence for agentic deployment
```

---

## Part 4 — AI Journey Eras (Shared Content)

Five eras. Industry-agnostic progression. Every edition references these unchanged; the edition may contextualize examples but the era model itself is fixed.

| era | name | window | signature | typical_posture |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ERA-01 | Automate | 2015–2020 | RPA, rules engines, BI dashboards | Completed at most enterprises |
| ERA-02 | Augment | 2020–2023 | ML in production; embedded analytics | Leaders have this; others fragmented |
| ERA-03 | Generative | 2023–2025 | LLM copilots; generative content; conversational surfaces | Actively deploying |
| ERA-04 | Agentic | 2025–2027 | Orchestrated agent fleets; HITL gates; autonomous exception handling | APEX's operating zone |
| ERA-05 | Adaptive | 2027+ | Self-learning fleets; cross-domain autonomous planning | Research and early pilots |

**File:** `apex-core/data/ai-journey-eras.json`
**Rule:** Editions must not redefine eras. They may contextualize examples under each era in their own edition-specific content.

---

## Part 5 — Commercial Maturity Model (Shared Content)

Five stages. Industry-agnostic progression. Every edition references these unchanged; the edition may define industry-specific signals for each stage.

| stage | name | data_posture | agent_posture | operations_posture |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CMM-1 | Foundations | ERP + core systems integrated to a data lake; basic BI | No production agents | Reactive, manual exception handling |
| CMM-2 | Connected | Real-time unified fabric; API-first; canonical schemas emerging | Isolated ML models in production | Alerting on exceptions; dashboards primary |
| CMM-3 | Intelligent | Full canonical schemas in Gold; MLOps mature; copilots deployed | Generative copilots; 1–3 agents | Detection automated; resolution mostly human |
| CMM-4 | Agentic | Schemas + ORCHs + MCP tool catalog; agent fleet in production | 20+ agents; HITL gates defined | Resolution mostly autonomous; human touch for judgment |
| CMM-5 | Adaptive | Continuous-learning schemas; drift monitoring native | Fleet self-optimizes; cross-domain ORCHs | Adaptive operations |

**File:** `apex-core/data/cmm-stages.json`

### 5.1 Edition extensions

Each edition may define its own `cmm-signals.json` mapping CMM stages to industry-specific observable signals (e.g., "stockouts detected by customer complaints" for RC vs. "overbooking visible only at check-in" for TH). These signals are additive, not replacements.

---

## Part 6 — Reference Architecture (Shared Seven-Layer Model)

APEX is a seven-layer reference architecture. Microsoft-native by default. Every edition inherits the layer model; editions define industry-specific L1 source systems and L7 experiences.

| layer | name | primary_microsoft_services | function |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Edge & Source | *Edition-defined* (POS, PMS, CRS, core banking, etc.) | Origin systems emit events and state |
| L2 | Ingest & Integration | Fabric Data Factory, Event Hubs, IoT Hub, Synapse Link | CDC + streaming ingestion; API mediation |
| L3 | Storage | OneLake (Fabric), Azure Data Lake, ADX for telemetry | Bronze–Silver–Gold medallion |
| L4 | Semantic | Fabric Lakehouse + SQL endpoints; Power BI semantic models | Canonical schema registries |
| L5 | Intelligence | Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Search, embedding stores | Models, retrieval, evaluation harnesses |
| L6 | Orchestration | Azure AI Agent Service (DAG orchestrator), Logic Apps, Durable Functions | ORCH-01 through ORCH-12 execution |
| L7 | Experience | D365 Customer Insights, Copilot, Power Platform, Teams, custom frontends | Where humans and agents collaborate |

### 6.1 Cross-cutting (shared across all editions)

- **Identity & Access:** Entra ID, Purview for data governance, customer-managed keys
- **Observability:** Application Insights, Fabric monitoring, custom agent telemetry
- **Evals & Safety:** Azure AI Foundry evals, red-team harness, PII detection
- **Independence posture:** Client-tenant data planes; no Deloitte-side retention of client-identifiable data

## Part 7 — Canonical Schemas (Convention, Not Content)

Core defines **how** schemas are shaped. Editions define **what** schemas exist and **what entities** populate them.

### 7.1 Schema naming convention

- Each schema is an edition-specific 4–5 letter uppercase code ending in `L` or `ML`
- `<DOMAIN>ML` means "<Domain> Machine Learning schema"
- Examples from editions: MERML (Merchandising), SCML (Supply Chain), HOSML (Hospitality), REVML (Revenue Management)
- Each edition defines 3–5 schemas

### 7.2 Medallion assignment

Every schema entity is assigned to Bronze, Silver, or Gold:

| layer | purpose | exit_criteria_to_next |
|---|---|---|
| Bronze | Raw ingested, immutable, source-system schemas preserved | Schema conformance + quality thresholds + lineage complete |
| Silver | Cleansed, conformed, canonical schema applied, PII tokenized | Foreign keys resolve + canonical envelope validates + retention classified |
| Gold | Business-ready, denormalized, agent-consumable | Agent contract tests pass + BI semantic layer coverage + latency SLO met |

### 7.3 Entity template (applies to every schema entity in every edition)

```
entity_name         CAPS_SNAKE_CASE
layer               Bronze | Silver | Gold
scd2                Y | N
grain               natural-language grain description
primary_key         column list
columns             name | type | nullable | description | pii_class
foreign_keys        FK relationships
retention           retention policy class
tool_bindings       MCP tool IDs that read/write this entity
```

### 7.4 Canonical event envelope (shared across ALL editions)

Every Silver-layer event entity in every edition uses this envelope. This is **immutable**. Editions add payload structure; editions do not redefine the envelope.

```
event_id           UUID                -- primary key
event_ts           TIMESTAMPTZ (UTC)
event_type         VARCHAR(64)         -- controlled vocabulary, per-schema enum
entity_id          VARCHAR(32)         -- edition-contextual (store_id, property_id, account_id, etc.)
product_id         VARCHAR(32)         -- nullable
lot_id             VARCHAR(32)         -- nullable, SGTIN or equivalent
customer_id        VARCHAR(32)         -- tokenized, nullable
business_step      VARCHAR(32)         -- EPCIS-compatible controlled vocabulary
disposition        VARCHAR(32)         -- EPCIS-compatible controlled vocabulary
source_system      VARCHAR(32)
source_system_ts   TIMESTAMPTZ
payload            JSONB
pii_tokenized      BOOLEAN
```

**Rationale:** The shared envelope is what makes cross-edition analytics possible. A client that uses APEX-RC for retail and APEX-TH for its hotel subsidiary can correlate events across both estates because the envelope is identical.

### 7.5 Gold view naming convention

- Format: `GV_<SCOPE>_<PURPOSE>`
- Scope examples: `STORE`, `PROPERTY`, `CUSTOMER`, `CHAIN`, `CATEGORY`
- Every edition documents its Gold views as contracts, not materialized entities

---

## Part 8 — Orchestration & Tool Conventions

### 8.1 ORCH numbering

Every edition defines **12 canonical orchestrations** numbered `ORCH-01` through `ORCH-12`. Specific assignments are edition-defined. The numbering is consistent across editions as a **positional slot**, not a semantic guarantee — ORCH-05 in APEX-RC is Recall Impact; ORCH-05 in APEX-TH is Disruption Recovery. They share a slot position, not a meaning.

### 8.2 Orchestration contract template

Every ORCH in every edition declares:

```
orch_id
domain
agents              [list]
trigger             event spec
inputs              [gold_view | schema_entity]
tool_bindings       [mcp_tool_id]
hitl_gates          [gate_type + decision_surface + decision_attrib]
outputs             [artifact | event | state_change]
success_slo         time + quality thresholds
observability       telemetry + eval harness references
```

### 8.3 HITL gate types (shared taxonomy)

Four gate types. Every edition uses these; no edition may define additional types without amending Core.

| gate_type | description |
|---|---|
| HITL | Decision required, human-in-the-loop. Agent surfaces decision-ready brief; human approves, modifies, or rejects. |
| ACK_ONLY | No decision required, visibility only. Human acknowledges autonomous action. |
| ZERO_TOUCH | Fully autonomous. Surfaces to human only on exception or SLO breach. |
| ESCALATION | Deferred to higher authority (legal, compliance, comms, exec). Local human initiates handoff rather than decides. |

### 8.4 MCP tool naming convention

Format: `mcp.<domain>.<capability>.<action>`

Domain codes are edition-specific but share structural properties:

- Lowercase, dot-separated
- Always scoped (e.g., `mcp.store.*`, `mcp.property.*`, not bare top-level)
- Action verbs are declarative (`resolve`, `detect`, `assemble`, `stage`)

### 8.5 Tool contract template

```
tool_id             mcp.<domain>.<capability>.<action>
binds_to            Gold view OR Silver entity OR external API
purpose             single-sentence description
request_schema      JSON schema
response_schema     JSON schema
auth                identity + scope requirement
idempotency         idempotent | non-idempotent
side_effects        read-only | writes | external-invoke
observability       latency SLO + error taxonomy
```

---

## Part 9 — Design System (Shared)

Every edition site uses this design system. Editions may extend tokens (e.g., add a unique industry accent color); editions may not break theme behavior, typography stack, or component patterns.

### 9.1 Typography

- **Display:** Fraunces (Google Fonts, variable, opsz 9–144)
- **Body:** Instrument Sans (Google Fonts, variable 400–700)
- **Mono:** JetBrains Mono (Google Fonts, variable 300–700)

**Forbidden as primary:** Inter, Roboto, Arial, system-ui. Fallback only.

### 9.2 Color tokens (dark theme, default)

```css
--bg-void:       #060a12
--bg-surface:    #0b111e
--bg-card:       #121a2c
--bg-card-hi:    #1a2339
--line:          #1e2a44
--line-hi:       #2f3f5f
--text:          #e7ecf7
--text-dim:      #8a97b2
--text-mute:     #56627c
--amber:         #f5a623    /* HITL / decision surface */
--teal:          #2dd4bf    /* agent / autonomous / schema */
--crimson:       #ef4444    /* severity: critical */
--slate:         #64748b    /* severity: low */
--gold:          #d4a244    /* outcome / commercial */
--indigo:        #7c83de    /* platform foundation (APEX-unique) */
```

### 9.3 Color tokens (light theme, warm paper)

```css
--bg-void:       #f4efe3
--bg-surface:    #ebe4d3
--bg-card:       #ffffff
--bg-card-hi:    #faf5e9
--line:          #dbd1b9
--line-hi:       #b8aa8c
--text:          #1a1f2e
--text-dim:      #4a5060
--text-mute:     #847d68
--amber:         #8f5a0c
--teal:          #0d7d70
--crimson:       #a81616
--slate:         #525b6e
--gold:          #8a6508
--indigo:        #3e4894
```

Light theme is warm cream + crisp white cards, not a flat white inversion. Semantic meaning preserved across themes.

### 9.4 Edition accent extension

Each edition may add **one** industry-accent token for differentiation:

- APEX-RC: `--rc-accent: #d4a244` (gold — retail heritage)
- APEX-TH: `--th-accent: #2a9d8f` (teal-jade — travel horizon)
- APEX-FS: `--fs-accent: #4f46e5` (indigo-deep — finance gravitas) (reserved)

The edition accent shows up in the masthead wordmark and one signature visual moment per edition site. It does not replace the shared semantic palette.

### 9.5 Theme initialization (shared, mandatory)

Every edition site must:

1. Include an inline `<script>` in `<head>` that reads `localStorage.getItem('apex-theme')`, falls back to `prefers-color-scheme`, sets `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` before CSS loads. No flash.
2. Render a theme toggle pill in the masthead top-right (sun icon in dark mode, moon in light, label swap).
3. Use a 280ms ease-out transition on `background-color`, `color`, `border-color`, `box-shadow` when the toggle fires.
4. Persist the choice to `localStorage` under key `apex-theme`.

### 9.6 Layout architecture (shared)

- Max width 1280px, 48px padding (28px at <960px)
- Sticky top nav with anchors to major parts
- Hero masthead with edition wordmark in Fraunces, live status pill, theme toggle
- Part-by-part content with large Fraunces section numbers
- Footer with version, date, internal classification

### 9.7 Architecture diagram style (shared)

Layered architecture boxes rendered as:

- Layered gradient boxes (4–6% luminance shift top to bottom)
- Stacked with 8px vertical gaps
- Depth via 1px top highlight and 1px bottom shadow borders (not drop shadows)
- Accent inner-left border in the appropriate semantic color per layer
- JetBrains Mono labels top-left with layer code (e.g., `L3 · STORAGE`)

### 9.8 Motion (shared)

- CSS-only preferred
- Live-dot pulse on "Live" status chips (2s infinite)
- Hover transitions 150–200ms
- Tab switches 200ms cross-fade
- Honor `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`

## Part 10 — Reusable Render Components

Core ships a set of framework-agnostic widgets. Editions consume them and pass edition-specific JSON.

| widget | file | contract | consumes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Theme toggle | `/js/theme.js` | Auto-mounts on `.theme-toggle` | `localStorage['apex-theme']` |
| Navigation | `/js/navigation.js` | Anchor scroll + sticky nav behavior | HTML structure |
| Solution Stack Chart | `/js/solution-stack.js` | Filterable, sortable, faceted table | `solution-stack.json` |
| ORCH Expander | `/js/orch-expander.js` | Click-to-expand ORCH contract detail | `orchestrations.json` |
| Wave Timeline | `/js/wave-timeline.js` | Horizontal wave timeline with hover exit criteria | `waves.json` |
| CMM Filter | `/js/cmm-filter.js` | Filter content by CMM stage | `cmm-stages.json` + edition content |
| Domain Tabs | `/js/domain-tabs.js` | Switch between edition's domain views | `agents.json` grouped by domain |
| Architecture Diagram | `/js/arch-diagram.js` | Render seven-layer diagram from layer + component data | `solution-stack.json` filtered to infrastructure |

### 10.1 Widget contract principle

Every Core widget is a pure function of its input JSON. Editions produce JSON; widgets render. No widget hard-codes industry content. This is what makes the framework extensible — a new edition (FS, LS, etc.) inherits all widgets for free by shaping its JSON to the Core contract.

## Part 11 — Acceptance Criteria for Editions

A new APEX edition is Core-conformant when:

1. Folder exists as `apex-<code>/` parallel to `apex-core/`
2. Edition README declares its code, full name, and Core spec version referenced
3. Edition defines **6–10 Forces of Change** conforming to Part 3 template
4. Edition references Parts 4 (Eras) and 5 (CMM) unchanged from Core
5. Edition defines **3–5 canonical schemas** using Part 7 naming and entity template
6. Every Silver-layer event entity uses the Part 7.4 canonical envelope unchanged
7. Edition defines **12 orchestrations** (ORCH-01 through ORCH-12) with Part 8.2 contracts
8. Edition defines its MCP tool catalog using Part 8.4 naming convention
9. Edition site uses Core design system (Part 9) with at most one accent token addition
10. Edition site consumes Part 10 reusable widgets; does not reimplement them
11. Edition passes Part 0 compliance check (no forbidden terminology anywhere)
12. Edition Solution Stack JSON has ≥50 rows conforming to the Part 13 shape
13. Edition defines at least one reference implementation under `apex-<code>/ref-impl/`

---

## Part 12 — Wave-Based Deployment Model (Convention)

Core defines the wave convention; editions populate wave content.

### 12.1 Convention

- Every edition defines exactly **4 waves**: W1 Foundation, W2 Expansion, W3 Platform, W4 Adaptive
- Each wave is self-funding (W1 ROI funds W2, etc.)
- Each wave has defined entry posture, scope, exit criteria, expected economics
- Edition-specific durations and economics

### 12.2 Wave contract template

```
wave_id              W1 | W2 | W3 | W4
name                 VARCHAR
scope                 domains + entities + agents + orchestrations
entry_posture        required CMM stage + infrastructure baseline
exit_criteria        [criterion + metric + threshold + measurement_method]
typical_duration     months
expected_economics   uplift_source + size_band + payback_window
next_wave_prerequisite
```

---

## Part 13 — Solution Stack (Shape Convention)

Every edition produces a Solution Stack — the flat, denormalized ~50-row table that binds every layer of the framework into one addressable grid.

### 13.1 Required columns (every edition)

| column | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| row_id | VARCHAR | Stable identifier |
| layer | ENUM | L1 / L2 / L3 / L4 / L5 / L6 / L7 |
| domain | ENUM | Edition-defined domain codes + PLATFORM |
| component_name | VARCHAR | Human-readable name |
| component_type | ENUM | service / entity / agent / orch / tool / isv / experience |
| ref_arch_code | VARCHAR | e.g., `L3.MERML.STORE_INVENTORY_POSITION`, `L6.ORCH-04` |
| microsoft_service | VARCHAR | Primary Microsoft service binding |
| isv_binding | VARCHAR | Optional ISV component |
| wave_availability | ENUM | W1 / W2 / W3 / W4 |
| cmm_stage_required | ENUM | CMM-1 through CMM-5 |
| agent_bindings | ARRAY | Referenced agents |
| tool_bindings | ARRAY | Referenced MCP tools |
| gold_view_produces | ARRAY | Gold views this component composes |
| description | TEXT | One-paragraph description |

### 13.2 Row target

~50 rows at full build, composed of ~7 infrastructure, ~4 schema registries, ~4 Gold view categories, ~30+ agents (edition-defined count), ~12 ORCH definitions, plus experience and ISV bindings.

## Part 15 — Build Sequence for Claude Code

Four phases. Core builds before any edition consumes it.

### Phase 1 — Conventions & design system
**Deliverables:**
- `/conventions/*.md` — all convention docs
- `/design-system/*.css` — tokens, typography, components, diagrams
- `/data/ai-journey-eras.json`, `/data/cmm-stages.json`

**Acceptance:**
- All convention docs readable as standalone references
- CSS passes AA contrast in both themes
- Typography loads with preconnect, no FOUT in production build

### Phase 2 — Reusable widgets
**Deliverables:**
- `/js/theme.js` — theme toggle with localStorage + prefers-color-scheme fallback
- `/js/navigation.js` — sticky nav + anchor scrolling
- Basic widget stubs for solution-stack, orch-expander, wave-timeline

**Acceptance:**
- Widgets mount on standardized CSS selectors (e.g., `.theme-toggle`, `.solution-stack`)
- Each widget consumes edition JSON via `fetch` or `data-src` attribute
- Widgets degrade gracefully if JSON is missing

### Phase 3 — Full widget implementation
**Deliverables:**
- Complete Solution Stack Chart with filter + sort + facet + row-detail panel
- Complete ORCH Expander with contract-detail reveal
- Complete Wave Timeline with hover exit criteria
- Complete CMM Filter + Domain Tabs + Architecture Diagram

**Acceptance:**
- All widgets demo-able against Core-provided sample JSON
- Keyboard navigation supported on all widgets
- `prefers-reduced-motion` honored

### Phase 4 — Edition validation harness
**Deliverables:**
- `/tools/validate-edition.js` — script that checks an edition's folder against Part 11 acceptance criteria
- `/tools/lint-compliance.js` — scans edition content for Part 0 forbidden terminology

**Acceptance:**
- Running `validate-edition apex-rc/` returns pass/fail per acceptance criterion
- Running `lint-compliance apex-th/` flags any occurrence of forbidden terms in markdown, JSON, HTML, or JS

## Part 16 — Handoff Notes to Claude Code

**Core is built once and extended rarely.** Editions change frequently; Core changes slowly. Treat Core changes with version-bump discipline and update every downstream edition's spec version reference.

**Every convention has a template doc.** When an edition author has a question about a convention, they read the convention doc in `apex-core/conventions/`. The edition spec (RC, TH) should not re-explain Core conventions — it should reference them.

**Widgets are pure functions of JSON.** If a widget starts carrying industry-specific logic, that's a design break. Push industry logic down into the edition's data, not up into shared code.

**The lint tool in Phase 4 is the compliance backstop.** Run it before every edition deliverable goes out. Part 0 is too important to rely on manual review.

**When editions disagree with Core, Core wins.** If an edition wants to change the HITL taxonomy, the ORCH numbering, the event envelope, or the medallion exit criteria, that's a Core amendment, not an edition override. Propose the amendment, bump Core version, update every downstream edition.
